questions.q: What is the area of the parallelogram whose sides are represented by the vectors $\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$ and $2\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$?
questions.solution:
Let $\vec{a} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$.

The area of the parallelogram with adjacent sides $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ is given by $|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|$.

$\vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} \text{ and } \hat{j} \text{ and } \hat{k} \\ 1 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } 3 \\ 2 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 2 \end{vmatrix}$

$= \hat{i}(4 - 3) - \hat{j}(2 - 6) + \hat{k}(1 - 4)$

$= \hat{i} + 4\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$

The magnitude of the cross product is:

$|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}| = \sqrt{1^2 + 4^2 + (-3)^2}$

$= \sqrt{1 + 16 + 9} = \sqrt{26}$

The area of the parallelogram is $\sqrt{26} square units.

Answer: \sqrt{26}$ square units

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\vec{p} = \vec{a} - \vec{b}$, $\vec{q} = \vec{a} + \vec{b}$. If $|\vec{a}| = |\vec{b}| = 2$ and $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = 2$, then what is the value of $|\vec{p} \times \vec{q}|$?
questions.solution:
$\vec{p} \times \vec{q} = (\vec{a} - \vec{b}) \times (\vec{a} + \vec{b})$

$= \vec{a} \times \vec{a} + \vec{a} \times \vec{b} - \vec{b} \times \vec{a} - \vec{b} \times \vec{b}$

Since $\vec{a} \times \vec{a} = \vec{0}$, $\vec{b} \times \vec{b} = \vec{0}$, and $\vec{b} \times \vec{a} = -\vec{a} \times \vec{b}$:

$\vec{p} \times \vec{q} = 2(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$

$|\vec{p} \times \vec{q}| = 2|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|$

Using Lagrange's identity:

$|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|^2 = |\vec{a}|^2 |\vec{b}|^2 - (\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b})^2$

Substituting the given values $|\vec{a}| = 2$, $|\vec{b}| = 2$, and $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = 2$:

$|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|^2 = (2)^2 (2)^2 - (2)^2$

$|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|^2 = 16 - 4 = 12$

$|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}| = \sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3}$

Therefore, $|\vec{p} \times \vec{q}| = 2(2\sqrt{3}) = 4\sqrt{3}$

Answer: $4\sqrt{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Passage: Let $\vec{a}\times\vec{b}=\vec{c}$ and $\vec{b}\times\vec{c}=\vec{a}$.

Question: Consider the following statements :
I. $(\vec{a}\times\vec{b})\cdot\vec{c}+(\vec{b}\times\vec{c})\cdot\vec{a}=(\vec{c}\times\vec{a})\cdot\vec{b}$
II. $\{(\vec{a}\times\vec{b})\times(\vec{b}\times\vec{c})\}\cdot\vec{b}=1$
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.solution:
Given $\vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \vec{c}$ and $\vec{b} \times \vec{c} = \vec{a}$.

Taking the dot product of the first equation with $\vec{c}$:
$(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{c} = \vec{c} \cdot \vec{c} \Rightarrow [\vec{a} \vec{b} \vec{c}] = |\vec{c}|^2$

Taking the dot product of the second equation with $\vec{a}$:
$(\vec{b} \times \vec{c}) \cdot \vec{a} = \vec{a} \cdot \vec{a} \Rightarrow [\vec{b} \vec{c} \vec{a}] = |\vec{a}|^2$

Using the properties of the scalar triple product, $[\vec{a} \vec{b} \vec{c}] = [\vec{b} \vec{c} \vec{a}] = [\vec{c} \vec{a} \vec{b}]$.
Thus, $|\vec{a}|^2 = |\vec{c}|^2 = [\vec{a} \vec{b} \vec{c}]$.

Evaluating Statement I:
The left-hand side is $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{c} + (\vec{b} \times \vec{c}) \cdot \vec{a} = [\vec{a} \vec{b} \vec{c}] + [\vec{b} \vec{c} \vec{a}] = 2[\vec{a} \vec{b} \vec{c}]$.
The right-hand side is $(\vec{c} \times \vec{a}) \cdot \vec{b} = [\vec{c} \vec{a} \vec{b}] = [\vec{a} \vec{b} \vec{c}]$.
For the statement to be true, $2[\vec{a} \vec{b} \vec{c}] = [\vec{a} \vec{b} \vec{c}] \Rightarrow [\vec{a} \vec{b} \vec{c}] = 0$, which implies $|\vec{c}|^2 = 0$. This is not generally true for non-zero vectors. Hence, Statement I is incorrect.

Evaluating Statement II:
Substituting the given cross products into the expression:
$\{(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \times (\vec{b} \times \vec{c})\} \cdot \vec{b} = (\vec{c} \times \vec{a}) \cdot \vec{b} = [\vec{c} \vec{a} \vec{b}] = [\vec{a} \vec{b} \vec{c}] = |\vec{c}|^2$
This expression equals $1$ only if $|\vec{c}| = 1$. Since there is no condition restricting the magnitude of $\vec{c}$ to $1$, Statement II is also incorrect.

Therefore, neither Statement I nor Statement II is correct.

Answer: Neither I nor II

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Passage: Let $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$, $\vec{c}$, $\vec{a}+\vec{b}$, $\vec{b}+\vec{c}$, $\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}$ be unit vectors.

Question: What is the angle between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ ?
questions.solution:
Given $|\vec{a}| = 1$, $|\vec{b}| = 1$, and $|\vec{a}+\vec{b}| = 1$.

Squaring the magnitude of $\vec{a}+\vec{b}$, we get:

$|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|^2 = |\vec{a}|^2 + |\vec{b}|^2 + 2|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|\cos\theta$

Substituting the given values:

$1^2 = 1^2 + 1^2 + 2(1)(1)\cos\theta$

$1 = 2 + 2\cos\theta$

$2\cos\theta = -1$

$\cos\theta = -\dfrac{1}{2}$

$\theta = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Passage: Let $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$, $\vec{c}$ be unit vectors. Further, $\vec{a}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{b}$; $\vec{c}$ makes an angle $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ with both $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$; and $\vec{c}=p\vec{a}+q\vec{b}+r(\vec{a}\times\vec{b})$.

Question: What is the value of $r^2$ ?
questions.solution:
Given $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$, $\vec{c}$ are unit vectors, so $|\vec{a}| = |\vec{b}| = |\vec{c}| = 1$.

Since $\vec{a}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{b}$, $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = 0$.

The vector $\vec{c}$ makes an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ with both $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$, giving $\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a} = 1 \cdot 1 \cdot \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $\vec{c} \cdot \vec{b} = 1 \cdot 1 \cdot \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

We are given $\vec{c} = p\vec{a} + q\vec{b} + r(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$.

Taking the dot product of $\vec{c}$ with $\vec{a}$:

$\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a} = p(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{a}) + q(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a}) + r((\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{a})$

$\dfrac{1}{2} = p(1) + q(0) + r(0) \Rightarrow p = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Taking the dot product of $\vec{c}$ with $\vec{b}$:

$\vec{c} \cdot \vec{b} = p(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}) + q(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{b}) + r((\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{b})$

$\dfrac{1}{2} = p(0) + q(1) + r(0) \Rightarrow q = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Taking the dot product of $\vec{c}$ with itself:

$|\vec{c}|^2 = p^2|\vec{a}|^2 + q^2|\vec{b}|^2 + r^2|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|^2$

Since $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are orthogonal unit vectors, $|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}| = |\vec{a}||\vec{b}|\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 1$.

Substituting the values:

$1 = p^2 + q^2 + r^2$

$1 = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 + r^2$

$1 = \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{4} + r^2$

$r^2 = 1 - \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Passage: Let $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$, $\vec{c}$, $\vec{a}+\vec{b}$, $\vec{b}+\vec{c}$, $\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}$ be unit vectors.

Question: What is the angle between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{c}$ ?
questions.solution:
Given $|\vec{a}| = |\vec{b}| = |\vec{c}| = 1$

$|\vec{a}+\vec{b}| = 1 \Rightarrow |\vec{a}|^2 + |\vec{b}|^2 + 2\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = 1 \Rightarrow 1 + 1 + 2\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = 1 \Rightarrow \vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$

$|\vec{b}+\vec{c}| = 1 \Rightarrow |\vec{b}|^2 + |\vec{c}|^2 + 2\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c} = 1 \Rightarrow 1 + 1 + 2\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c} = 1 \Rightarrow \vec{b}\cdot\vec{c} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$

$|\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}| = 1 \Rightarrow |\vec{a}|^2 + |\vec{b}|^2 + |\vec{c}|^2 + 2(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} + \vec{b}\cdot\vec{c} + \vec{c}\cdot\vec{a}) = 1$

$1 + 1 + 1 + 2\left(-\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} + \vec{c}\cdot\vec{a}\right) = 1$

$3 + 2(-1 + \vec{c}\cdot\vec{a}) = 1$

$1 + 2\vec{c}\cdot\vec{a} = 1 \Rightarrow \vec{c}\cdot\vec{a} = 0$

Since the dot product of $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{c}$ is $0$, the angle between them is $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A force $\vec{F} = 2\hat{i} - \lambda\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$ is applied at the point $A(1, 2, 5)$. If its moment about the point $B(-1, -2, 3)$ is $16\hat{i} - 6\hat{j} + 2\lambda\hat{k}$, then what is the value of $\lambda$?
questions.solution:
The position vector of the point of application $A$ with respect to point $B$ is $\vec{r} = \vec{r}_A - \vec{r}_B$.

$\vec{r} = (1 - (-1))\hat{i} + (2 - (-2))\hat{j} + (5 - 3)\hat{k} = 2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$

The moment of the force about point $B$ is given by $\vec{M} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F}$.

$\vec{M} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} \text{ and } \hat{j} \text{ and } \hat{k} \\ 2 \text{ and } 4 \text{ and } 2 \\ 2 \text{ and } -\lambda \text{ and } 5 \end{vmatrix}$

$\vec{M} = \hat{i}(20 + 2\lambda) - \hat{j}(10 - 4) + \hat{k}(-2\lambda - 8)$

$\vec{M} = (20 + 2\lambda)\hat{i} - 6\hat{j} - (2\lambda + 8)\hat{k}$

It is given that $\vec{M} = 16\hat{i} - 6\hat{j} + 2\lambda\hat{k}$.

Comparing the coefficients of $\hat{i}$ and $\hat{k}$:

$20 + 2\lambda = 16 \Rightarrow 2\lambda = -4 \Rightarrow \lambda = -2$

$-2\lambda - 8 = 2\lambda \Rightarrow 4\lambda = -8 \Rightarrow \lambda = -2$

Both equations yield $\lambda = -2$.

Answer: $-2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Passage: Let $\vec{a}\times\vec{b}=\vec{c}$ and $\vec{b}\times\vec{c}=\vec{a}$.

Question: Consider the following statements :
I. $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$, $\vec{c}$ are orthogonal in pairs.
II. $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$, $\vec{c}$ are unit vectors.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.solution:
Given $\vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \vec{c}$ and $\vec{b} \times \vec{c} = \vec{a}$.

From the properties of the cross product, $\vec{c}$ is perpendicular to both $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$.

Similarly, $\vec{a}$ is perpendicular to both $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$.

This implies that $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$, and $\vec{c}$ are mutually orthogonal. Thus, Statement I is correct.

Since the vectors are mutually orthogonal, the angle between any two of them is $90^{}^{\circ}$.

Taking the magnitude of the first equation:

$|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}| = |\vec{c}| \Rightarrow |\vec{a}||\vec{b}| = |\vec{c}|$

Taking the magnitude of the second equation:

$|\vec{b} \times \vec{c}| = |\vec{a}| \Rightarrow |\vec{b}||\vec{c}| = |\vec{a}|$

Substituting $|\vec{c}|$ from the first equation into the second:

$|\vec{b}|(|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|) = |\vec{a}| \Rightarrow |\vec{a}||\vec{b}|^2 = |\vec{a}|$

For non-zero vectors, we get $|\vec{b}|^2 = 1 \Rightarrow |\vec{b}| = 1$.

This gives $|\vec{a}| = |\vec{c}|$. However, $|\vec{a}|$ and $|\vec{c}|$ can be any positive real number and are not necessarily equal to $1$.

Thus, Statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $ABC$ is a triangle right-angled at $B$. If $A(k, 1, -1)$, $B(2k, 0, 2)$ and $C(2+2k, k, 1)$ are the vertices of the triangle, then what is the value of $k$?
questions.solution:
The direction ratios of the line segment $AB$ are $(k - 2k, 1 - 0, -1 - 2) = (-k, 1, -3)$.

The direction ratios of the line segment $BC$ are $(2+2k - 2k, k - 0, 1 - 2) = (2, k, -1)$.

Since the triangle is right-angled at $B$, the line segments $AB$ and $BC$ are perpendicular to each other.

Therefore, the dot product of their direction ratios is zero.

$(-k)(2) + (1)(k) + (-3)(-1) = 0$

$-2k + k + 3 = 0$

$k = 3$

Answer: $3$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following statements in respect of a vector $\vec{d} = (\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \times \vec{c}$:
I. $\vec{d}$ is coplanar with $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$.
II. $\vec{d}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{c}$.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Given $\vec{d} = (\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \times \vec{c}$

Using the vector triple product expansion:

$\vec{d} = (\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c})\vec{b} - (\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c})\vec{a}$

This shows that $\vec{d}$ is expressed as a linear combination of $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$. Thus, $\vec{d}$ lies in the plane containing $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$, making it coplanar with $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$. Statement I is correct.

By the definition of the cross product, the vector resulting from the cross product of two vectors is perpendicular to both of them. Since $\vec{d}$ is the cross product of $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$ and $\vec{c}$, it must be perpendicular to both $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$ and $\vec{c}$.

Therefore, $\vec{d} \cdot \vec{c} = 0$, which means $\vec{d}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{c}$. Statement II is correct.

Both statements I and II are correct.

Answer: Both I and II

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The position vectors of three points $A$, $B$ and $C$ are $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ respectively such that $3\vec{a} - 4\vec{b} + \vec{c} = \vec{0}$. What is $AB : BC$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $3\vec{a} - 4\vec{b} + \vec{c} = \vec{0}$

Rearranging the terms:

$3\vec{a} - 3\vec{b} = \vec{b} - \vec{c}$

$-3(\vec{b} - \vec{a}) = -(\vec{c} - \vec{b})$

Using the definition of position vectors, $\overrightarrow{AB} = \vec{b} - \vec{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{BC} = \vec{c} - \vec{b}$:

$-3\overrightarrow{AB} = -\overrightarrow{BC}$

$\overrightarrow{BC} = 3\overrightarrow{AB}$

Taking the magnitude on both sides:

$|\overrightarrow{BC}| = 3|\overrightarrow{AB}|$

$BC = 3AB$

$\dfrac{AB}{BC} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Thus, $AB : BC = 1 : 3$.

Answer: $1:3$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The position vectors of three points $A$, $B$ and $C$ are $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ respectively, where $\vec{c} = (\cos^2\theta)\vec{a} + (\sin^2\theta)\vec{b}$. What is $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) + (\vec{b} \times \vec{c}) + (\vec{c} \times \vec{a})$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $\vec{c} = (\cos^2\theta)\vec{a} + (\sin^2\theta)\vec{b}$

Substituting the value of $\vec{c}$ in the second term of the expression $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) + (\vec{b} \times \vec{c}) + (\vec{c} \times \vec{a})$:

$\vec{b} \times \vec{c} = \vec{b} \times ((\cos^2\theta)\vec{a} + (\sin^2\theta)\vec{b})$

$\vec{b} \times \vec{c} = (\cos^2\theta)(\vec{b} \times \vec{a}) + (\sin^2\theta)(\vec{b} \times \vec{b})$

Since $\vec{b} \times \vec{b} = \vec{0}$ and $\vec{b} \times \vec{a} = -(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$:

$\vec{b} \times \vec{c} = -(\cos^2\theta)(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$

Substituting the value of $\vec{c}$ in the third term:

$\vec{c} \times \vec{a} = ((\cos^2\theta)\vec{a} + (\sin^2\theta)\vec{b}) \times \vec{a}$

$\vec{c} \times \vec{a} = (\cos^2\theta)(\vec{a} \times \vec{a}) + (\sin^2\theta)(\vec{b} \times \vec{a})$

Since $\vec{a} \times \vec{a} = \vec{0}$:

$\vec{c} \times \vec{a} = -(\sin^2\theta)(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$

Adding the three terms together:

$(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) + (\vec{b} \times \vec{c}) + (\vec{c} \times \vec{a}) = (\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) - (\cos^2\theta)(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) - (\sin^2\theta)(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$

$= (\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) [1 - (\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta)]$

Using the trigonometric identity $\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1$:

$= (\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) [1 - 1]$

$= \vec{0}$

Answer: $\vec{0}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\theta$ be the angle between two unit vectors $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$. If $\vec{a}+2 \vec{b}$ is perpendicular to $5 \vec{a}-4 \vec{b}$, then what is $\cos \theta+\cos 2 \theta$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Since, $(\vec{a}+2 \vec{b}) \ \text{$ and $} (5 \vec{a}-4 \vec{b})$ are perpendicular vectors.
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow(\vec{a}+2 \vec{b}) \cdot(5 \vec{a}-4 \vec{b})=0 \\
& \Rightarrow 5|\vec{a}|^2-4 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+10 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}-8|\vec{b}|^2=0 \\
& \Rightarrow 5 \times 1+6 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}-8=0 \quad \text{ Since, }|\vec{a}|=|\vec{b}|=1 \\
& \Rightarrow 6|\vec{a}||\vec{b}| \cos \theta=3 \\
& \Rightarrow 1 \cdot 1 \cos \theta=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \cos \theta=\frac{1}{2}
\end{aligned}$
So, $\cos 2 \theta=2 \cos ^2 \theta-1=2 \times \frac{1}{4}-1=-\frac{1}{2}$
Now, $\cos \theta+\cos 2 \theta=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}=0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $3 \alpha+2 \beta$ equal to if $(2 \hat{i}+6 \hat{j}+27 \hat{k}) \times(\hat{i}+\alpha \hat{j}+\beta \hat{k})$ is a null vector?
questions.solution:
Given that, $(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+6 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+27 \hat{\mathrm{k}}) \times(\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\alpha \hat{\mathrm{j}}+\beta \hat{\mathrm{k}})=0\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\
2 & 6 & 27 \\
1 & \alpha & \beta
\end{array}\right|=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \hat{i}(6 \beta-27 \alpha)-\hat{j}(2 \beta-27)+\hat{k}(2 \alpha-6)=0
\end{aligned}$
Comparing both sides of above equation, we get:-
$\begin{aligned}
& 6 \beta-27 \alpha=0 \Rightarrow 2 \beta=9 \alpha \\
& 2 \beta-27=0 \Rightarrow \beta=\frac{27}{2} \text{ and } 2 \alpha-6=0 \Rightarrow \alpha=3
\end{aligned}$
So, $3 \alpha+2 \beta=3 \times 3+2 \times \frac{27}{2}=9+27=36$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$, $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$ be unit vectors. What is $(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b})$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $|\vec{a}| = 1$, $|\vec{b}| = 1$, and $|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}| = 1$.

Using Lagrange's identity, $|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|^2 + (\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b})^2 = |\vec{a}|^2 |\vec{b}|^2$.

Substituting the given values, $1^2 + (\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b})^2 = 1^2 \times 1^2$.

$1 + (\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b})^2 = 1$.

$(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b})^2 = 0 \Rightarrow \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = 0$.

Answer: $0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let ABCDEF be a regular hexagon. If $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AD}}=m \overrightarrow{\mathrm{BC}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{CF}}=n \overrightarrow{\mathrm{AB}}$, then what is $m n$ equal to?
questions.solution: In a regular hexagon, $\begin{aligned} & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{AB}}=2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{FC}} \\ & \Rightarrow \overrightarrow{\mathrm{AB}}=-2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{CF}} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{n}=-2 \end{aligned}$ Also, $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AD}}=2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{BC}}\therefore \quad \mathrm{m}=2$ Now, $m n=2(-2)=-4$

questions.q:
The vectors $\vec{a}, \vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ are of the same length. If taken pairwise, they form equal angles. If $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}$ and $\vec{b}=\hat{j}+\hat{k}$, then what can $\vec{c}$ be equal to?
A. $\hat{i}+\hat{k}$
B. $\frac{-\hat{i}+4 \hat{j}-\hat{k}}{3}$
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution:
Given that,
$\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}, \vec{b}=\hat{j}+\hat{k}$
Since, $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$ has same length.
$\Rightarrow|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}|=|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}|=|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}|=\sqrt{1+1}=\sqrt{2}$
Let $\theta$ be the angle between the vectors.
$\therefore \cos \theta=\frac{\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}}{|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|}=\frac{0+1+0}{\sqrt{2} \times \sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{2}\because$ All the conditions are satisfied, so it can be vector $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}$
(I) Take $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}} \Rightarrow|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}|=\sqrt{1+1}=\sqrt{2}$ and $\cos \theta=\frac{\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}}{|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}||\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}|}=\frac{1+0+0}{\sqrt{2} \sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{2}$ All $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}$ the conditions are satisfied. So, it can be vector.
(II) Take $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=\frac{\hat{\mathrm{i}}+4 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-\hat{\mathrm{k}}}{3} \Rightarrow|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}|=\frac{1}{3} \sqrt{1+16+1}=\frac{3 \sqrt{2}}{3}=\sqrt{2}$ and $\cos \theta=\frac{\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}}{|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}||\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}|}=\frac{\frac{-1}{3}+\frac{4}{3}}{\sqrt{2} \sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{2}\because$ All the conditions are satisfied, so it can be vector $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are two vectors of magnitude 4 inclined at an angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$, then what is the angle between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{a}-\vec{b}$ ?
questions.solution:
The angle between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{a}-\vec{b}$ is given by
$\cos \theta=\frac{\vec{a} \cdot(\vec{a}-\vec{b})}{|\vec{a}||\vec{a}-\vec{b}|}$

Passage: Let $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$, $\vec{c}$ be unit vectors. Further, $\vec{a}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{b}$; $\vec{c}$ makes an angle $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ with both $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$; and $\vec{c}=p\vec{a}+q\vec{b}+r(\vec{a}\times\vec{b})$.

Question: What is the value of $(p+q)$ ?
questions.solution:
Given $|\vec{a}| = |\vec{b}| = |\vec{c}| = 1$ and $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = 0$.

Since $\vec{c}$ makes an angle $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ with both $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$:

$\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a} = |\vec{c}||\vec{a}|\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\vec{c} \cdot \vec{b} = |\vec{c}||\vec{b}|\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

We are given the relation:

$\vec{c} = p\vec{a} + q\vec{b} + r(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$

Taking the dot product of both sides with $\vec{a}$:

$\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a} = p(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{a}) + q(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a}) + r((\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{a})$

Since $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{a} = 1$, $\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a} = 0$, and $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{a} = 0$, we get:

$p = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Taking the dot product of both sides with $\vec{b}$:

$\vec{c} \cdot \vec{b} = p(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}) + q(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{b}) + r((\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{b})$

Since $\vec{b} \cdot \vec{b} = 1$, $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = 0$, and $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{b} = 0$, we get:

$q = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Therefore, $p + q = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} = 1$.

Answer: $1$

questions.solution:
Let point $\mathrm{A}=(5,2), \mathrm{B}=(6,-15)$ and $\mathrm{O}=(0,0)$.
Slope of line $\mathrm{OA}=m_1=\frac{2-0}{5-0}=\frac{2}{5}$
Slope of line $\mathrm{OB}=m_2=\frac{-15-0}{6-0}=\frac{-15}{6}$
Angle between two lines with slopes $m_1 and m_2$ is
$\begin{aligned}
\tan (\theta) & =\frac{m_1-m_2}{1+m_1 \cdot m_2} \\
& =\frac{\frac{2}{5}-\left(-\frac{15}{6}\right)}{1+\frac{2}{5} \cdot\left(-\frac{15}{6}\right)}=\frac{\frac{2}{5}+\frac{15}{6}}{1-1} \\
\tan (\theta) & =\infty \Rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{2}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: What is the value of $\lambda$ for which the vectors $\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}$, $2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}, \quad \lambda \hat{i}-\hat{j}+\lambda \hat{k}$, are coplanar?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & x(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})+y(2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k})=\lambda \hat{i}-\hat{j}+\lambda \hat{k} \\ & \Rightarrow(x+2 y) i+(-x+y) \hat{j}+(x-y) \hat{k}=\lambda \hat{i}-\hat{j}+\lambda \hat{k} \\ & x+2 y=\lambda \\ & 3 y=0, x=\lambda \\ & y=0, \lambda=1\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $P Q R S$ is a parallelogram, where $\overrightarrow{P Q}=3 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}-m \hat{k}$, $\overrightarrow{P S}=\hat{i}+3 \hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and the area of the parallelogram is $\sqrt{90}. What is the value of $m$ ?$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text{ Area$ of $parallelogram }=\frac{1}{2}|(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{PQ}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{PS}})| \\ & \therefore \sqrt{90}=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 3 & 2 & -m \\ 1 & 3 & 1\end{array}\right| \\ & =[\hat{i}(2+3 m)-\hat{j}(3+m)+\hat{k}(9-2)] \\ & \sqrt{90}=\sqrt{(2+3 m)^2+(3+m)^2+49} \\ & =\sqrt{4+12 m+9 m^2+9+m^2+6 m+49} \\ & \sqrt{90}=\sqrt{10 m^2+18 m+62}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \sqrt{90}=\sqrt{10 m^2+18 m+62} \\ \Rightarrow & 10 m^2+18 m+62-90=0 \\ \Rightarrow & 10 m^2+18 m-28=0 \\ \Rightarrow & 5 m^2+9 m-14=0 \\ \Rightarrow & 5 m^2-5 m+14 m-14=0 \\ & 5 m(m-1)+14(m-1)=0 \\ & m-\frac{14}{5}, m=1\end{aligned}$
